quote: the hour that turns back longing
note: Dusk on Easter Sunday, the end of the first day on the mountain. These are among the best-loved lines of the poem: evening as the hour of homesickness. The souls here are travelers too, far from the home they are bound for.
The evening bell that rang for Compline, the Church's last prayer of the day.
Christians prayed facing east, toward the rising sun, a symbol of Christ.

"Before the ending of the light": the Latin hymn of Compline. It asks God to keep watch through the night, and to hold back bad dreams and "our enemy". The prayer is about to be answered in front of Dante.

Dante stops to tell the reader that what follows is allegory. What it means is still argued. The serpent cannot really harm these saved souls, so the scene is usually read as a nightly ritual: a reminder that against temptation they depend wholly on God's help.
Blunted swords. Usually read as weapons for defense only, or as God's justice tempered with mercy. Others say the points are gone because the battle with the devil is already won.
Green is the color of hope, the virtue of everyone on this mountain.

context: The angels come from the highest heaven, where she sits. The souls have just sung to her for help.
Dante, who probably knew him, is relieved to find him saved. The cry suggests he had feared otherwise.

note: Nino takes Dante for a dead soul like himself. The saved are ferried to the mountain across the ocean in an angel's boat (Canto 2).
The life of the body. "The other" is eternal life, which Dante hopes this journey will win him.
Nino's only child, a girl of about nine in 1300. He trusts her prayers because she is innocent.
Beatrice d'Este, of the ruling family of Ferrara. Four years after Nino's death she married Galeazzo Visconti of Milan. Nino's remarks about women are those of a hurt husband.
Widows wore black, with white bands on the head. Putting them aside meant marrying again.
Another prophecy after the event. In 1302 the Visconti were driven out of Milan, and Beatrice shared her new husband's years of exile.
The coat of arms of the Visconti of Milan: a viper swallowing a child. The Milanese army pitched camp where this banner was raised.

Nino's own arms as ruler of Gallura, a rooster. Carved on her tomb, it would have shown her a faithful widow, a better honor than the viper. Despite the shared name, Nino's family and the Visconti of Milan were not related.
The south pole of the sky. Stars near a pole turn in small circles, like the hub of a wheel. Purgatory lies in the southern hemisphere, so these are stars no one in Europe sees.
Usually read as the three virtues that come by grace: faith, hope and charity.

The stars of Canto 1, usually read as the four virtues of the active life: prudence, justice, courage and temperance. They rule the day, the time for action. The three rule the night, the time for prayer.
The serpent of Genesis 3, who tempted Eve to eat the forbidden fruit in Eden. This flowering valley is a small, unsafe Eden. The real one waits at the top of the mountain.
The two angels. The serpent runs at the mere sound of their wings: there is no fight.
The valley of the river Magra, in the Lunigiana, the hill country where Tuscany meets Liguria. It was the Malaspina family's land.

context: He has stared at Dante all through the angels' flight. His first thought, even here, is for news of home.

note: The elder Currado was his grandfather, who founded this branch of the family.

quote: that love which here grows pure
note: His fault, as he sees it: he cared so much for his family and its greatness that he neglected God. On the mountain that love is cleansed and turned the right way.
True in 1300. Exile would take Dante there a few years later.
In Italian, the purse and the sword: open-handedness and courage, the two virtues of a noble house. This is Dante's thanks to the family that sheltered him.
Dante's words are "the guilty head". Most readers take it as the pope, Boniface VIII, or as Rome under the popes. Some take it as the devil.

The sun is in the Ram, Aries, each spring, so this means before seven years have passed. In 1306 Dante, an exile, was the guest of the Malaspina in the Lunigiana and acted as their envoy in a peace treaty. He will learn their generosity by experience, not hearsay.
